prompt: A slide at the park makes a right triangle with the ground and the ladder post. One angle is the right angle, and the slide meets the ground at $55^\circ$. What is the third angle, in degrees?
hint: The three angles of ANY triangle add up to $180^\circ$.

hints.text: The three angles of ANY triangle add up to $180^\circ$.
The right angle already uses $90^\circ$, so the other two must share $90^\circ$.

explanation: The right angle takes $90^\circ$, leaving $90^\circ$ for the other two.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the slide tipping
steps: A very steep slide meets the ground near $90^\circ$ and leaves almost nothing at the top.
A gentle slide meets the ground near $0^\circ$ and leaves almost $90^\circ$ at the top.
